title: How to create a useful daily brief with AI
description: Use AI to bring together your calendar, messages, meetings, tasks, and current work into a short brief for the day ahead.
introduction: Most daily briefs are easy to generate and hard to use. They repeat the calendar, summarize a few messages, and leave you to decide which items are connected and what actually deserves attention.

A better brief does some of that judgment before the day gets busy. Strawberry can check the browser tabs, logged-in tools, connected apps, meeting records, and files where the day is already taking shape, then bring together the meetings, promises, deadlines, messages, blockers, and changes that could affect your plan. The underlying sources stay close enough to check.

blocks.text: The point of a daily brief is to help you decide how to use the day. A long list of everything that changed overnight is usually worse than a short view of the few things that may alter a priority, require preparation, or block someone else.
emphasis: decide how to use the day

blocks.text: Strawberry can check the selected calendar, communication, task, project, and meeting sources together. If a meeting note says you promised a draft today, the project record still has no owner, and the relevant email thread has gone quiet, those are parts of one situation rather than three unrelated notifications. Your brief can show the connection and link back to each source.

items.context: Prepare a concise, source-linked view of the priorities, meetings, messages, risks, and decisions that need attention today.

sections.title: Start with the context you already have

blocks.text: You do not need to connect every company system before the first run. Strawberry can begin with an open calendar, a few relevant tabs, uploaded files, meeting notes, or the apps that are already available. When another connection would materially improve the result, your companion can explain what it would add instead of turning the morning into a setup project.

items: The outcomes and decisions that deserve focus today.
The meetings or schedule changes that need preparation.
The messages, promises, or blockers that need attention.
A short watch list, including any sources that disagree.

sections.title: Use the brief to make the next decision

blocks.text: The brief may reveal that one inbox needs a proper pass, a particular meeting needs deeper preparation, or a commitment has fallen between the meeting notes and the project tracker. Strawberry can carry the relevant context into that next workflow, so you are not starting again from a blank chat.
emphasis: not starting again from a blank chat

items.title: Go deeper on the inbox
items.text: Process the communication queue that needs replies, delegation, a decision, or cleanup.

skill.context: Process the communication queue that needs deeper attention, replies, delegation, or cleanup.

items.title: Resolve a commitment that fell between tools
items.text: Reconcile the evidence, owner, and smallest useful next step when the status is unclear.

skill.context: Reconcile commitments and ownership when the evidence is spread across several systems.

blocks.text: A recommendation is still different from an action. Your companion can prepare a reply, task change, delegation, or calendar adjustment from the brief, while leaving the actual send or system change for the appropriate review.

sections.title: Make later briefs feel like yours

blocks.text: The first brief gives you something concrete to correct. You can say which sources are dependable, what was missing, what did not deserve space, and how much detail helps. Strawberry can carry those preferences forward without treating one unusual morning as a permanent rule.

Once the method is reliable, it can become a Routine for the workdays and destination you choose. It can check the agreed sources and prepare the brief at the right time, while messages, calendar changes, assignments, and other external actions stay within the review behavior you approved.
